# Authentication

Build a `Client` from one of the four Box auth flows. Each flow is an `Auth`
the runtime uses to fetch a bearer token; the network layer refreshes on a
`401` and retries once. The flow builders live in the `auth` namespace (JWT on
the Node-only `./jwt` subpath) and are passed straight to `new Client(...)`.

## Developer Token

A fixed token from the Developer Console, for quick local testing:

```ts
import { auth } from '@unofficialbox/box-open-sdk';
const client = new Client(auth.developerToken('DEVELOPER_TOKEN'));
```

## Client Credentials Grant (server auth, no key)

Set exactly one subject — `enterpriseId` for the service account, or `userId`
to act as a managed user:

```ts
import { auth } from '@unofficialbox/box-open-sdk';
const client = new Client(auth.clientCredentials({
  clientId: 'CLIENT_ID',
  clientSecret: 'CLIENT_SECRET',
  enterpriseId: 'ENTERPRISE_ID',
}));
```

## JWT (server auth with a signing key)

Parses (and if needed decrypts) the RSA key up front, so a bad key fails
loudly at construction. It reaches `node:crypto`, so it is a Node-only leaf
imported from the runtime's `./jwt` entry point and returns a promise:

```ts
import { jwtAuth } from '@unofficialbox/box-open-sdk/jwt';
const auth = await jwtAuth({
  clientId: 'CLIENT_ID',
  clientSecret: 'CLIENT_SECRET',
  publicKeyId: 'PUBLIC_KEY_ID',
  privateKeyPem: privateKeyPem, // optionally encrypted; set passphrase
  enterpriseId: 'ENTERPRISE_ID',
});
const client = new Client(auth);
```

## OAuth 2.0 (authorization code)

Redirect the user to the authorize URL, exchange the returned code, then reuse
the rotated refresh token on later runs (persist it via `onRefresh`):

```ts
import { auth } from '@unofficialbox/box-open-sdk';
// later runs: resume from the stored refresh token.
const source = auth.oauth({ clientId: 'CLIENT_ID', clientSecret: 'CLIENT_SECRET' }, storedRefreshToken);
const client = new Client(source);
```

## Revoking a token

For logout or uninstall, `revokeToken()` revokes the token a CCG, JWT, or OAuth
flow holds — with the flow's own client credentials, at the revoke endpoint
beside its token URL, through its `fetch` — and clears it from the cache:

```ts
await source.revokeToken();
```

A CCG or JWT flow acquires a fresh token on its next use. OAuth revokes the
whole grant: every later call rejects, so discard the stored refresh token and
run the authorization-code flow again. A developer token has no client
credentials to revoke with — pass them yourself to
`client.authorization.revokeOauth2`.

## Acting as another user

An admin, or a service account whose app may *make API calls using the as-user
header*, can act as another user. `withAsUserHeader` returns a new client whose
every call sends Box's `As-User` header; it shares the original's auth (and
token cache) and configuration, and the original is unchanged:

```ts
const userClient = client.withAsUserHeader('USER_ID');
const me = await userClient.users.getMe(); // the user USER_ID
```

## Downscoping a token

Exchange the session's access token for one limited to `scopes` and,
optionally, to one item (its API URL) or shared link — e.g. to hand a
browser-side preview a narrow token. The result has no refresh token; build
a client from it as a developer token:

```ts
const down = await client.authorization.downscopeToken(
  ['item_preview'],
  'https://api.box.com/2.0/files/123',
);
const preview = new Client(auth.developerToken(down.access_token!));
```
